title: Feature vs conjunction search
summary: Treisman & Gelade (1980), Experiments I and II. The observer searches a card of 1 to 36 coloured letters for a target and presses one key if it is there and another if not. The target differs from the other letters by one feature (a blue letter or an S) or only by a conjunction of colour and shape (a green T among brown Ts and green Xs); Experiment II compares an easy and a difficult conjunction in letter matrices. The measure is reaction time against the number of letters. The paper reported nearly flat slopes for feature targets and steep linear slopes for conjunctions, with target-present slopes about half the target-absent ones. Tested in software and simulation only; no result of this implementation is claimed.
references: Treisman, A. M., & Gelade, G. (1980). A feature-integration theory of attention. Cognitive Psychology, 12(1), 97-136. https://doi.org/10.1016/0010-0285(80)90005-5
Treisman, A., Sykes, M., & Gelade, G. (1977). Selective attention and stimulus integration. In S. Dornic (Ed.), Attention and Performance VI (pp. 333-361). Erlbaum.

deviations.original: Hand-made cards with stencilled letters in coloured inks, shown in an Electronics Development three-field tachistoscope (Exp. I, p. 103) or a two-field Cambridge tachistoscope (Exp. II, p. 108)
deviations.here: A computer monitor; letters rendered from strokes in RGB colours on a white field, sized in degrees from the rig file's geometry
deviations.reason: Tachistoscopes and ink cards are not available; the display geometry, letters and timing are reproduced on a monitor.

deviations.original: The experimenter said "Ready" and pressed a button to show the fixation card (p. 103)
deviations.here: The subject presses SPACE on the plain white field
deviations.reason: No experimenter at a button; the subject-paced start keeps the plain white field before every trial.

deviations.original: Subjects were told their RT and whether they were correct after each trial (p. 103)
deviations.here: "Correct 512 ms" / "Error 640 ms" on the screen for 1.5 s
deviations.reason: Told on screen rather than by the experimenter.

deviations.original: One set of hand-placed cards per condition and display size, reused across blocks; positions "appeared random" (p. 102)
deviations.here: The deck is generated from the session seed with the paper's placement rules, new layouts for every block
deviations.reason: Procedural cards follow the stated rules exactly and are reproducible from the seed and each trial's row (the items column).

deviations.here: Written to the trials file with dummy = 1 and dropped by the notebook
deviations.reason: Keeping the rows costs nothing and shows that the procedure ran; the analysis excludes them as the paper did.

deviations.original: A digital timer started by the onset of the search card and stopped by the key (p. 103)
deviations.here: From the display flip that showed the array to the frame on which the key was read
deviations.reason: Monitor presentation: RT resolution is one frame plus the keyboard's latency.

deviations.here: The window's grey background shows for the frames between the end of feedback and the next white ready field
deviations.reason: alhazen blanks the display between trials; the ready field is up before the subject can start.
